name: CDL - Cyber Defense Lab
description: The UMBC Cyber Defense Lab is a place where students, faculty, and affiliates carry out cybersecurity research. Current projects include high-integrity voting, protocol analysis, and cybersecurity education.

name: CORAL - Cognition Robotics and Learning Lab
description: Research related to machine and human intelligence, including machine vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Current projects include sample efficient reinforcement learning, safe artificial intelligence, graph neural networks for anomaly detection, and multi-modal learning from images and text.

name: CREM - Center of Research in Emergent Manufacturing
description: Research in operational technology cybersecurity, medical devices, training and workforce development, and AI-enabled digital engineering tools. Current projects include a multi-cloud data sharing platform, 2D-3D engineering design conversion, AI-designed microfluidic systems, and GRC compliance tools for OT environments.

name: CVG - Cognitive Vision Group
description: Works on the conceptual characterization of visual scenes, broadly in computational perception, learning, and reasoning. Areas of focus include visual understanding under incomplete information, generalizing to new domains, and interpreting and predicting behavior.

name: DAMS - Data Management and Semantics
description: Focuses on Data Management, AI, Privacy, and the Internet of Things, bridging the gap between raw sensor data and semantically meaningful data. Builds prototypes and deploys them in the real world, incorporating semantics and privacy-awareness into system design.

name: DREAM - Discovery, Research, and Experimental Analysis of Malware Lab
description: Applies machine learning to cybersecurity and malware analysis, using techniques like tensor decomposition and string similarity measures. Home to UMBC's cyber defense competition team, the CyberDawgs.

name: Ebiquity Research Laboratory
description: Builds intelligent systems in open, heterogeneous, dynamic, distributed environments. Research topics include the semantic web, information extraction, mobile computing, privacy, and security. Co-directed with Dr. Tim Finin (finin@umbc.edu).

name: FSI - Future Sensing and Interaction Lab
description: Advances mobile, wearable, and ubiquitous computing, designing sensing systems for healthcare, human-computer interaction, and environmental sustainability. Integrates mobile computing, wireless and wearable sensing, and AI for IoT.

name: IRAL - Interactive Robotics and Language Laboratory
description: Research in robotics, human-robot interaction, and grounded language understanding, combining robotics, natural language processing, and statistical learning to build agents that interact robustly with non-specialists.

name: KAI2 - Knowledge-infused AI and Inference
description: Integrates AI with human knowledge represented as knowledge graphs, lexicons, process knowledge, and commonsense content, designing human-centered systems for sensitive domains. Works toward explainable, interpretable, and safe neuro-symbolic AI.

name: LARA Lab
description: Uses and improves language tools to build human-centered AI by studying how people communicate. Combines natural language processing, cognitive science, and AI to create agents that tell stories, play Dungeons & Dragons, and aid accessibility in human communication.

name: Social Intelligence Lab
description: Explores social computing topics, aiming to understand how people engage with complex systems and design user-centric platforms. Current focus areas include accessible health monitoring, equitable STEM education, and responsible use of large language models.

name: TAIC - Trustworthy and Intelligent Computing
description: Studies security and privacy issues with AI and collaborative systems, confidential computing, and applications of AI in science.

name: VANGOGH Lab
description: Covers computer graphics and animation research, including real-time graphics hardware techniques, visual appearance, data visualization, physics-based animation, and machine learning for natural phenomena. Co-directed with Dr. Marc Olano (olano@umbc.edu).

name: Vinjamuri Lab
description: Studies Brain-Machine Interfaces (BMIs) that control upper-limb prostheses, focusing on how the brain controls complex hand movements. Includes graduate, undergraduate, and high school students, with publications and patents dating back to 2014.

name: ECLIPSE Cluster
description: Comprises groups with shared laboratories, projects, and students: the Mobile, Pervasive, & Sensor Systems Laboratory led by Dr. Nilanjan Banerjee, and the Covail Analog & Digital Systems Research Laboratory, led by Dr. Ryan Robucci (robucci@umbc.edu).

name: ESNET - Embedded Systems and Networks Laboratory
description: Design and management of wireless sensor networks, network architecture and protocols, underwater communication, MAC and routing protocols, energy-aware system design, secure communication, fault tolerance, and topology management.

name: SECRETS - SECure, REliable, and Trusted Systems
description: Focuses on the design, security, trustworthiness, reliability, and testability of electronic chips, including hardware security, fault tolerance, machine learning for security, and lightweight authentication for IoT and medical devices.

name: VLSI-SOC Group
description: Research areas include Electronic Design and Automation, brain-inspired computing, neural network architecture exploration, autonomous driving and CAN security, mixed-signal CMOS ICs/SOCs, and CAD tools for microprocessor and FPGA design.

name: CASPR - Center for Advanced Studies in Photonics Research
description: Advanced photonics research and technology development in optical communications, optical sensing and devices, nanophotonics, biophotonics, and quantum optics.

name: Choa's Lab - Brain and Nanotech Research
description: Develops transcranial magnetic stimulation coils for brain stimulation, studies brain dynamics via EEG and fMRI, and builds neural network architectures. Also researches photonic and nano-materials, including single photon detectors, tunable lasers, and neuromorphic computing devices for AI chips.

name: Computational Photonics Laboratory
description: Computational and theoretical studies of nonlinear optics, RF photonics, and frequency combs, including soliton generation, supercontinuum generation, and machine learning to optimize photonic devices and systems. Assistant Director: Dr. Ergun Simsek (simsek@umbc.edu).

name: MLSP-Lab - Machine Learning for Signal Processing Laboratory
description: Develops theory and tools for processing signals across a range of applications, combining statistical and adaptive signal processing with machine learning, focused especially on medical image analysis and fusion.

name: Remote Sensing Signal and Image Processing Laboratory
description: Research on remote sensing, signal and image processing, specifically hyperspectral imaging, medical imaging, and automatic target recognition.

name: Bieberich Research Group
description: not found

name: Brewster Research Group
description: not found

name: Burns Arthropod Evolution (BAE) Lab
description: Studies the evolutionary and ecological mechanisms behind sexual conflict in animal mating systems, especially in harvesters (daddy-longlegs). Combines genomic sequencing, functional morphology, bioinformatics, and cytological methods.

name: Chugh Research Group (AMB Lab)
description: Director, Applied Molecular Biology (AMB) Program

name: Elizondo Lab
description: Studies how immune dysfunction breaks down tissue integrity and glucose homeostasis in diabetes using transgenic mouse models. Techniques include flow cytometry, CRISPR gene editing, single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, qPCR, ELISA, and fluorescence microscopy.

name: Freeland Lab
description: Studies how and why evolution arrived at 20 amino acids for decoding genetic information. Uses computers to build and study amino acid structures beyond the standard genetic code, with a focus on astrobiology and the origin of life.

name: Gardner Lab
description: Studies bacterial metabolism and physiology, using Cellvibrio japonicus to learn how microbes detect, degrade, and consume polysaccharides. Combines transcriptomics, proteomics, bacterial genetics, and biochemistry, and designs 3D printed devices for growth experiments.

name: Green Research Group
description: not found

name: Kann Lab
description: Builds computational methods to study disease mutations and protein interactions, including databases of disease mutations mapped to protein domains. Undergraduate teams from biology and computer science build text-mining tools that extract mutations and protein interactions from biomedical literature. Some projects require no programming experience.

name: LeGates Lab
description: Studies how neurons integrate information to regulate behaviors related to depression, such as reward and cognitive function. Combines electrophysiology, imaging, and behavior in mice.

name: Leips Lab
description: Studies the genetic basis of natural variation in aging using Drosophila melanogaster. Uses genetic mapping, genomics, and functional approaches. Current projects focus on age-related changes in immunity, reproduction, and physical performance.

name: Weihong Lin Lab
description: Studies chemical sensory systems in the nose, including detection of e-cigarette flavors and sensory dysfunction from chemical exposure. Uses genetically modified mice, calcium imaging, electrophysiological recordings, immunolabeling, and behavioral assays.

name: Lobo Lab
description: Reverse engineers the mechanisms that control biological growth and form. Combines computational methods, mathematical models, and bioinformatics with bench experiments to study development, regeneration, cancer, and synthetic biology.

name: Lohr Lab
description: Studies bird hearing and song. Projects include how far songbirds can detect and recognize songs in noise, Grasshopper Sparrow song variation and breeding behavior, sexual selection and birdsong, and comparative hearing across bird species.

name: Lu Research Group
description: not found

name: Mendelson Lab
description: Studies the causes and consequences of behavioral evolution using North American freshwater fish called darters. Projects cover mate choice, male breeding color, reproductive isolation, and phylogenies built from molecular markers.

name: Miller Lab
description: Uses the green alga Volvox carteri to study how cells differentiate and how that evolved. Projects cover how asymmetric cell divisions are regulated and how the somatic cell fate is maintained.

name: Omland Lab
description: Studies avian evolution, ecology, behavior, and conservation, with a focus on New World orioles. Recent work covers female coloration, female song, and the Puerto Rican Oriole. Prospective students are invited to email about the Puerto Rico work or related projects.

name: Padmanabhan Lab
description: Studies how normal cells become cancerous, how cancer cells grow, evade the immune system, and metastasize, and how to build more effective cancer therapies. Uses molecular, cellular, and organismic tools.

name: Robinson Lab
description: Studies phototransduction, how light in the environment becomes a biological signal.

name: Schreier Laboratory
description: Studies nitrogen and sulfur cycles in marine recirculating aquaculture systems and nitrogen fixation in the gut of a wood-eating catfish. Based at the Institute of Marine and Environmental Technology in Baltimore.

name: Starz-Gaiano Laboratory
description: Uses fruit flies (Drosophila) to find the genes and physical features of tissues that control cell migration, which matters for animal development and human disease.

name: Sutton Lab
description: Studies G protein coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling in the brain and how disruptions contribute to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disease. Uses behavioral phenotyping, proteomics, imaging, and cell-based assays.

name: The Vonhoff Lab
description: Uses the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster to study neuroscience, from basic science to neurological diseases, including developmental mechanisms and aging-dependent degeneration. Students can pick a project or propose their own if it can be studied in the Drosophila nervous system.

name: The Walker Lab at UMBC
description: Studies how exosomes reprogram cells to drive breast cancer metastasis, with projects on metastatic initiation, breast cancer dormancy in bone marrow, and tissue repair and regeneration.

name: Cronin Lab
description: Studies the visual physiology of invertebrates, especially mantis shrimp, including color vision, polarized-light signals, and the molecular genetics of opsins. Also studies how many other animals evolved vision suited to their environments.

name: Lamas Lab
description: Visiting Researcher; honey bee biology and disease

name: Polymeric Biomaterials Lab
description: Polymeric-based biomaterials for therapeutics, cell manufacturing, and tissue repair.

name: Blaney Lab
description: Fate/impact of pharmaceuticals in wastewater and environmental remediation.

name: AMEE Lab
description: not found

name: Frey Lab
description: Bioprocess engineering, chromatographic separations of recombinant protein.

name: Garcia Lab

name: Ghosh Lab
description: Analysis and remediation of toxic pollutants in soils and sediments.

name: Hennigan Lab
description: Atmospheric chemistry and aerosol pollution processes.

name: JB Lab
description: Engineered platforms/systems biology for immune dysfunction in cancer and infectious disease.

name: ATOMS Lab (AI & Theory-Oriented Molecular Science)
description: Molecular simulation and machine learning for chemistry.

name: Marten Lab
description: Bioprocess engineering, systems biology of gene regulatory networks. Department Chair.

name: Rao Lab / CAST
description: Bioprocess engineering, sensor development; Director of Center for Advanced Sensor Technology (CAST).

name: Welty Lab / CUERE
description: Groundwater-surface water hydrology, urban watershed processes; Director of CUERE.

name: Family Adversity Lab
description: Effects of PTSD/trauma on family relationships; resilience among trauma survivors.

name: Child Development Lab
description: Executive functioning and attention regulation and their impact on learning.

name: CACHE Lab (Cognition, Affect, and Cardiometabolic Health Lab)
description: Biopsychosocial factors in cardiometabolic disease risk, aging, and health disparities.

name: EQUIPS Lab
description: Validation/development of psychosis spectrum assessments.

name: UMBC Home Visiting Training Center
description: Social development in infancy; early family interventions supporting families in poverty.

name: Children and Families, Schooling and Development Lab
description: Factors promoting academic success; children's math and literacy development.

name: ACED Lab (Affect, Cognition, & Emotional Disorders Lab)
description: Interaction between cognition and emotion in emotional disorders.

description: A math and statistics consulting service run by the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. Supports interdisciplinary research in the biological sciences, engineering, and social sciences, and gives students consulting experience as research assistants.

name: Lu Research Group
description: Computational mechanics and materials science, including reduced order modeling and data-driven methods for high-performance computing, multi-scale modeling of materials and additive manufacturing, fracture mechanics, and digital image correlation.

name: Human-Centered Computing Program
description: Studies how humans interact with technology, in the Department of Information Systems. Offers study at the undergraduate, masters, and PhD level. Enrolled undergraduates can email the Graduate Program Director to join a mailing list for HCC events, internships, and job opportunities.
